disclaimer: Estimates only. Not affiliated with any agency or utility. Not tax, legal, or benefits advice – consult a tax professional for tax credits. Official agencies decide eligibility. Coverage is incomplete; CalClaim emphasizes California state benefits over federal ones.

programs.name: Medi-Cal
programs.oneLiner: Low- or no-cost health coverage
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$400/mo coverage value (estimate; varies)
applySteps: Apply at Covered California or BenefitsCal
Provide income and household info
Upload ID / proof of income if asked

programs.name: CalFresh
programs.oneLiner: Monthly grocery benefits (SNAP)
programs.maxBenefit: Up to FFY2026 USDA max allotment for household size (estimate)
applySteps: Apply on BenefitsCal
Report household and income
Complete interview if required
Submit documents if requested

programs.name: WIC
programs.oneLiner: Food and nutrition support for pregnancy / young kids
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$52/mo cash-value food voucher (estimate; full food package value is often higher and varies by category)
applySteps: Find your local WIC agency
Schedule an appointment
Bring ID and proof of income / categorical enrollment

programs.name: SSI
programs.oneLiner: Federal disability / aged income support
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $994/mo federal SSI for an individual (2026; estimate)
applySteps: Start at SSA SSI application
Provide medical and financial information
Attend interview if scheduled

programs.name: CalWORKs
programs.oneLiner: Cash aid and employment services for families with kids
programs.maxBenefit: Up to county MAP cash aid by household size (estimate)
applySteps: Apply via BenefitsCal or your county
Complete interview
Submit income and household documents
If approved, your county may require Welfare-to-Work (WtW) employment services

programs.name: CAPI
programs.oneLiner: State cash aid for aged, blind, or disabled non-citizens ineligible for SSI/SSP solely due to immigration status
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$1,234/mo SSI/SSP-equivalent for an individual (Jan 2026 CAPI standard; estimate)
applySteps: Apply via BenefitsCal or your county social services agency (SOC 814)
Show SSI/SSP denial (or proof of ineligibility) based on immigration status alone
Provide ID, residency, income, and resource documents
Complete county interview if scheduled

programs.name: GA/GR
programs.oneLiner: County General Assistance / General Relief cash aid for adults who do not qualify for other state or federal cash programs
programs.maxBenefit: County-set; often ~$200–$400/mo for a single adult (LA GR ~$221; estimate – varies by county)
applySteps: Apply via BenefitsCal or your county social services agency
Expect strict income/resource limits and a county residency check
Complete interview; employable adults may need work registration
In Los Angeles County, employable GR clients may be referred to GROW job services

programs.name: CMSP
programs.oneLiner: Temporary health coverage for low-income adults (21–64) in participating CMSP counties who are not eligible for other coverage
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$400/mo coverage value (estimate; county CMSP / Connect to Care packages vary)
applySteps: Apply for health benefits via BenefitsCal or your county – they screen Medi-Cal and CMSP together
Provide residency, income, and resource verification if asked

programs.name: Disaster CalFresh
programs.oneLiner: Temporary food benefits after a federally declared disaster – only when your county opens a D-CalFresh application window
programs.maxBenefit: Up to one month at the CalFresh max allotment for household size (estimate; disaster window only)

deadlines.label: Only during county Disaster CalFresh application windows after a declared disaster

applySteps: Apply during your county's Disaster CalFresh window only – by phone or in person, as your county announced
Show you lived or worked in the disaster area at the time of the disaster
Report a disaster-related loss (food, income, inaccessible resources, or disaster expenses)

programs.name: LifeLine
programs.oneLiner: Phone or internet discount for the person named on the account
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$19/mo phone or internet discount (CA LifeLine estimate)
applySteps: Confirm you qualify via income or categorical program
Apply online or through your provider
Keep approval letter

programs.name: CARE
programs.oneLiner: Utility bill discount for the person named on the bill (PG&E, SDG&E, SCE, or SoCalGas)
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$70/mo off electric (≈35% of ~$200 bill; estimate)
applySteps: Apply online through your utility's CARE page
Have your utility account number or recent bill ready

programs.name: FERA
programs.oneLiner: Electric bill discount if CARE income is a bit too high (PG&E, SDG&E, or SCE)
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$36/mo off electric (≈18% of ~$200 bill; estimate)
applySteps: Use your utility's CARE/FERA application (electric IOUs only)
Have account number or recent bill ready

programs.name: ESA
programs.oneLiner: Free home energy upgrades through your utility
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$3,000 in free upgrades (estimate; utility measures)
applySteps: Apply or get referred through your utility ESA page
Schedule assessment if approved

programs.name: LIHEAP
programs.oneLiner: Help with heating/cooling bills (seasonal; county-run)
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$1,500 one-time bill help (estimate; county/season/benefit type)
applySteps: Find your local LIHEAP provider via CSD
Apply during open window
Bring ID, income proof, and utility bill

programs.name: AMP (Arrearage Management)
programs.oneLiner: Forgiveness path for past-due utility balances
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$8,000 debt forgiveness over 12 months of on-time payments (estimate; utility-specific)
applySteps: Confirm you have qualifying past-due balance
Enroll via utility assistance / AMP page
Keep on-time payments as required

programs.name: Medical Baseline
programs.oneLiner: Extra utility allowance if a resident needs power for a qualifying medical condition or device; bill must be in your name
programs.maxBenefit: Extra ~500 kWh / 25 therms per month at the lowest baseline rate – worth roughly $50/mo (estimate; varies widely by rate plan and usage)
applySteps: Get medical practitioner certification
Submit Medical Baseline application to your utility

programs.name: LADWP EZ-SAVE
programs.oneLiner: Bill discount for income-qualified LADWP customers (electric, water, sewer)
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$40/mo off LADWP charges (estimate; varies by usage)
applySteps: Confirm you are the LADWP customer of record at your primary residence
Apply online for EZ-SAVE at ladwp.com/EZSAVE

programs.name: SMUD EAPR
programs.oneLiner: Monthly electric bill discount for income-qualified SMUD customers
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$105/mo off SMUD electric for the lowest-income tier (estimate)
applySteps: Check EAPR income guidelines on SMUD's low-income page
Apply online through My Account or download the mail-in application

programs.name: Unemployment Insurance
programs.oneLiner: Weekly cash benefit (up to $450/wk) if you lost your job through no fault of your own
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $450/wk for up to 26 weeks (2026; weekly cap unchanged since 2005)
applySteps: File a claim online at UI Online (edd.ca.gov)
Certify for benefits every two weeks
Show you're able, available, and actively looking for work

programs.name: State Disability Insurance (SDI)
programs.oneLiner: Weekly wage-replacement benefit if illness, injury, or pregnancy keeps you from working
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $1,765/wk for up to 52 weeks (2026)
applySteps: File a Disability Insurance claim online (edd.ca.gov)
Have your doctor or practitioner certify your disability
Must be unable to work for at least 8 days and have SDI wages in your base period

programs.name: Paid Family Leave (PFL)
programs.oneLiner: Weekly wage-replacement benefit to bond with a new child or care for a seriously ill family member
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $1,765/wk for up to 8 weeks in a 12-month period (2026)
applySteps: File a Paid Family Leave claim online (edd.ca.gov)
Provide proof of the qualifying family event (birth, adoption, or a family member's serious illness)
Must have SDI wages in your base period

programs.name: In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS)
programs.oneLiner: Pays a caregiver (often a family member) to help an aged, blind, or disabled person stay safely at home
programs.maxBenefit: Averages about 100 hrs/mo of paid care statewide, at your county's hourly rate ($16.90-$23.00/hr) – roughly $1,700-$2,300/mo (estimate; depends on your assessed hours and county wage)
applySteps: Contact your county IHSS office to request an assessment
Usually requires (or is applied for alongside) Medi-Cal eligibility
A social worker assesses hours of care needed; you or a hired provider get paid for approved hours

programs.name: CalEITC
programs.oneLiner: Cash-back state tax credit for working Californians with low to moderate income
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $3,756 for tax year 2025 (3+ kids); up to $302 with no kids (income limit ~$32,900; figures adjust yearly)

deadlines.label: Tax year 2026 California filing deadline (2025 figures shown; amounts adjust annually)

applySteps: File a California state tax return (free help via VITA or CalEITC4Me)
Complete FTB Form 3514 with your return
Must have earned income (wages or self-employment) at or below the published limit

programs.name: Young Child Tax Credit (YCTC)
programs.oneLiner: Extra state tax credit for families with a child under 6, on top of CalEITC
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $1,189 for tax year 2025 (must also qualify for CalEITC; figures adjust yearly)

deadlines.label: Tax year 2026 California filing deadline (2025 figures shown; amounts adjust annually)

applySteps: File a California state tax return and qualify for CalEITC
Complete FTB Form 3514 with your return
Must have a qualifying child under age 6 at year end

programs.name: MyFirstEV
programs.oneLiner: Instant rebate on your first electric or hydrogen vehicle at participating dealers
programs.maxBenefit: $3,500 off a qualifying new ZEV (MSRP up to $50,000) or $1,750 off a used ZEV ($25,000 or less); CA-headquartered ZEV-only makers are exempt from the price caps

deadlines.label: While participating manufacturers still have funds (one-time appropriation; statutory spend-by Sep 1, 2031)

applySteps: Confirm the automaker is live – Hyundai, Lucid, and Tesla as of Aug 7, 2026; Ford, Chevrolet, Kia, and Rivian expected later in August; Toyota/Lexus, Honda, and Subaru in September; Mitsubishi in November; Nissan and Volvo TBD
Pick a qualifying battery-electric or hydrogen fuel-cell vehicle (not a plug-in hybrid) under the price cap, or a California-headquartered ZEV maker such as Lucid or Rivian
Complete CARB's first-time ZEV attestation (signed under penalty of perjury) and give the confirmation number to the dealer before you sign
Register the vehicle to a California address – the discount comes off the price at the dealership, not as a later tax credit

programs.name: SmartFlex Rewards
programs.oneLiner: $25 from PG&E if you connect a Nest or other smart thermostat so it can use a little less energy on the hottest days
programs.maxBenefit: $25 signup bonus (plus a chance at monthly prizes; estimate)
applySteps: Confirm the PG&E electric bill is in your name and you have a Wi-Fi Nest, other eligible smart thermostat, or eligible EV charger
Sign up at smartflexrewards.com
Keep the device on Wi-Fi. On a few very hot or cold days it may briefly use less energy — you can opt out of any day

programs.name: PG&E Pre-Owned EV Rebate
programs.oneLiner: Rebate for buying a qualifying used EV through PG&E's EV rebate portal
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $1,000 standard / up to $4,000 income-qualified (estimate; program rules)

deadlines.label: Standard pre-owned EV rebate applications due

applySteps: Confirm the used EV qualifies on PG&E's EV rebate portal
Apply at evrebates.pge.com before the deadline
Upload proof of purchase / registration as requested

programs.name: PG&E Residential EV Charging Rebate
programs.oneLiner: Rebate toward a Level 2 home EV charger / panel upgrades (PG&E EV Charge Network residential path)
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $5,000 for Plus / income-qualified paths (estimate; tier depends on eligibility)
applySteps: Confirm you are a PG&E residential electric customer buying or owning an EV
Apply on PG&E's residential EV charging rebate page
Install a qualifying charger and submit invoices as required

programs.name: PG&E Generator & Battery Rebate
programs.oneLiner: Rebate for a portable generator or battery for outage preparedness. Renters also qualify.
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $300 generator / up to $500 battery (estimate; PG&E program caps)
applySteps: Buy a qualifying generator or battery within the program window
Apply on PG&E's generator and battery rebate page
Upload receipt and account details

programs.name: Clean Cars 4 All
programs.oneLiner: Scrap an older car for a grant toward a cleaner vehicle or mobility options
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$12,000 toward a qualifying cleaner vehicle (estimate; air district rules)
applySteps: Confirm your air district still has Clean Cars 4 All funding
Scrap a qualifying older vehicle and apply through the district program
Use the grant toward an eligible EV / hybrid / alternative mobility option

programs.name: Driving Clean Assistance Program (DCAP)
programs.oneLiner: Point-of-sale grant for income-qualified Californians buying a cleaner vehicle
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$12,000 vehicle grant plus up to ~$2,000 charging / mobility add-ons (estimate)
applySteps: Check income and vehicle eligibility on CARB's DCAP page
Get pre-approved before purchasing
Complete the purchase at a participating dealer

programs.name: Foster Youth Tax Credit
programs.oneLiner: Extra California tax credit for former foster youth who also qualify for CalEITC
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $1,189 for tax year 2025 (figures adjust yearly; must also qualify for CalEITC)

deadlines.label: Tax year 2026 California filing deadline (2025 figures shown; amounts adjust annually)

applySteps: File a California return and qualify for CalEITC (FTB Form 3514)
Confirm you meet foster-youth age and foster-care timing rules
Claim the Foster Youth Tax Credit on the same Form 3514

programs.name: Premium Tax Credit (Covered California)
programs.oneLiner: Federal subsidy that lowers Covered California monthly premiums
programs.maxBenefit: Varies widely – often hundreds per month off marketplace premiums (estimate)
applySteps: Apply or renew at CoveredCA.com
Report household income for APTC / Premium Tax Credit
Reconcile the credit on your federal tax return (Form 8962)

programs.name: SUN Bucks (Summer EBT)
programs.oneLiner: Summer grocery benefit for school-age kids when school meals pause
programs.maxBenefit: $120 per eligible child for summer 2026 (estimate; CDSS publishes each year)

deadlines.label: Summer 2026 SUN Bucks application / issuance window ends

applySteps: Check if your child was auto-enrolled via school meal / CalFresh / Medi-Cal data
If not, apply on the CDSS SUN Bucks page before the seasonal deadline
Use benefits on an EBT card at authorized retailers

programs.name: Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI)
programs.oneLiner: Monthly disability benefit if you have enough work credits and meet SSA disability rules
programs.maxBenefit: Average ~$1,500/mo (individual amounts vary with earnings history; estimate)
applySteps: Apply online at ssa.gov or at a local Social Security office
Provide medical evidence and work history
Expect a multi-month decision; appeal if denied

programs.name: Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA)
programs.oneLiner: Short-term cash aid for refugees and other eligible newcomers not on CalWORKs
programs.maxBenefit: Up to CalWORKs-equivalent grants for up to 4 months (estimate; county-administered)
applySteps: Apply on BenefitsCal for Refugee Cash Assistance
Provide immigration / arrival documents
Aid is typically limited to the first months after arrival

programs.name: California Food Assistance Program (CFAP)
programs.oneLiner: State-funded food benefits for some immigrants who are income-eligible but not CalFresh-eligible
programs.maxBenefit: Same allotment scale as CalFresh for household size (estimate)
applySteps: Apply on BenefitsCal – CFAP uses the CalFresh application path
County determines federal CalFresh ineligibility due to immigration status
If CFAP-eligible, benefits issue on an EBT card

programs.name: California Nonrefundable Renters' Credit
programs.oneLiner: Small California tax credit if you paid rent on a CA home and meet income limits
programs.maxBenefit: $60 single / $120 joint or head of household (nonrefundable)
applySteps: File a California tax return
Claim the nonrefundable renters' credit if you paid qualifying rent
Keep rent receipts in case FTB asks

programs.name: Self-Generation Incentive Program (SGIP)
programs.oneLiner: Incentive for home battery storage (currently waitlisted / funds reserved)
programs.maxBenefit: Varies by system size and equity budget – often several thousand dollars when open (estimate)
applySteps: Check SGIP portal for open budget / waitlist status before applying
Work with an approved developer / installer
Submit reservation and claim paperwork through the SGIP portal

programs.name: HEEHRA (Home Electrification / HOMES path)
programs.oneLiner: Federal home electrification rebate path in California (funds fully reserved as of Feb 2026)
programs.maxBenefit: Up to several thousand toward qualifying electrification upgrades when open (estimate)
applySteps: Check California Energy Commission / contractor channels for reopen status
Do not apply expecting current funding – budgets were fully reserved Feb 24, 2026
If a waitlist or reopen is announced, follow the official contractor / portal path

programs.name: Tax credits (info)
programs.oneLiner: Federal/state credits you may claim at tax time (info path)
programs.maxBenefit: Up to ~$4,000/yr combined credits for some households (estimate)
applySteps: Gather income records and receipts (W-2s, 1099s, award letters)
Book a VITA / tax-preparer appointment – this usually means a real meeting
CalClaim does not file taxes

programs.name: Federal Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
programs.oneLiner: Federal cash-back credit for working people with low to moderate income
programs.maxBenefit: Up to about $8,046 for tax year 2025 with 3+ kids (estimate; IRS publishes annual tables)
applySteps: File a federal tax return (free help via VITA)
Claim EITC on Form 1040 / Schedule EIC if you have qualifying children
Must have earned income and meet IRS income limits

programs.name: Child Tax Credit (CTC)
programs.oneLiner: Federal tax credit per qualifying child under 17
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $2,200 per qualifying child (tax year 2025+; phaseout starts high)
applySteps: File a federal tax return listing each qualifying child
Claim the Child Tax Credit / Additional Child Tax Credit as applicable
Have SSNs for you and each qualifying child

programs.name: Child and Dependent Care Credit
programs.oneLiner: Federal credit for work-related child or dependent care expenses
programs.maxBenefit: Up to 35% of qualifying expenses (caps apply; estimate varies by income)
applySteps: Track qualifying care expenses and provider TINs
File Form 2441 with your federal return
Must have earned income and a qualifying child / dependent

programs.name: Saver's Credit
programs.oneLiner: Federal credit for contributing to an IRA or workplace retirement plan
programs.maxBenefit: Up to $1,000 single / $2,000 joint (estimate; rate depends on income)
applySteps: Contribute to a qualifying IRA or workplace plan
Claim the credit on Form 8880 with your federal return
Income must be under the IRS Saver's Credit limits

programs.name: 511 Contra Costa e-bike rebate
programs.oneLiner: After-purchase cash rebate for a new pedal e-bike if you live in Contra Costa County
programs.maxBenefit: $150 standard, or $300 if income-qualified (at or below 400% FPL)

deadlines.label: Apply within 6 months of purchase, while funds last

applySteps: Buy a new Class 1–3 e-bike or installed conversion kit with working pedals (scooters and e-motos do not qualify)
Apply at 511 CCTA within six months with ID, Contra Costa proof of address, sales receipt with tax, and a photo of the serial number
Income-qualified applicants can upload a public-assistance letter or tax return for the $300 tier

programs.name: Ava Bike Electric
programs.oneLiner: Lottery instant rebate on a new pedal e-bike for Alameda County residents and Ava customers in San Joaquin County
programs.maxBenefit: $400–$1,500 at participating shops ($1,000/$1,500 income-qualified; cargo/adaptive pays more); plus $250 safety gear for income-qualified riders

deadlines.label: Monthly drawings through 2027 (apply before 11:59 p.m. the day before the 4th Tuesday)

applySteps: Confirm you live in Alameda County, or are an Ava Community Energy customer in San Joaquin County (Tracy, Stockton, Lathrop, or unincorporated)
Apply online before purchase – eligible applicants are entered in the next three monthly drawings
If selected, redeem the instant rebate at a participating shop within 60 days on a Class 1–3 pedal e-bike (not a scooter)

programs.name: Clean Cars 4 All / DCAP e-bike option
programs.oneLiner: Up to $7,500 toward a pedal e-bike (or transit) if you scrap an older car – income-qualified
programs.maxBenefit: $7,500 mobility option (e-bike and/or transit) after retiring an eligible older vehicle; household income at or below 300% FPL

deadlines.label: Must be approved before you scrap the car or buy the e-bike; funding varies by air district

applySteps: This is not a walk-in e-bike coupon – you must have an eligible older vehicle to retire and be at or below 300% of the federal poverty level

Find your air district on CARB's Clean Cars 4 All page. Bay Area, South Coast (Replace Your Ride), San Diego, and San Joaquin Valley run their own programs; everywhere else uses the statewide Driving Clean Assistance Program (DCAP)
Get preapproved, then scrap the car through the program and use the mobility card or voucher for a Class 1–3 pedal e-bike (scooters do not qualify). Sacramento's district round is currently paused
